body:
I am writing this report from the vantage-point of a very committed, entrenched, and involved spectator. In tandem, I am a pivotal figure in the events which have transpired.
I will admit that this report has been written almost solely for my own personal closure and satisfaction.
I will end my foreword and begin as such with an introduction to myself, my partner, my environs, and how the so called Pains of Past and Present have all come to the point that they have in my life.
I am currently 18 years of age, living in New York City. I have a history of mental illness - schizophrenia with catatonic features, anxiety, depression, the gamut basically but with specific quirks. My interests include artistic expression, especially music and poetry, making my own such pieces, and language and/or linguistics. My partner, CK, lives a stone's throw from my current home. He is currently 15 years of age, and suffers from what is currently an unclear condition which includes mood features, intense anxiety, gender dysphoria, and simply a lot of suffering on his part. His interests include coding/programming, identity studies such as those of the gender or rights of a being, and morbid fascinations (harmless, of course) such as true crime.
We live in a not-to-be-named area of New York City which happens to be among the highest-ranked places on the planet for underage (and otherwise) use of hard recreational drugs. These include, most commonly and most infamously, heroin, prescription pills (with the most popular being Xanax), K2 or Spice of various less-than-legitimate 'brand' names, and with a slightly smaller emphasis on party drugs such as 'molly' (whatever that means is dictated by who you are buying from and how much they care about you/themselves and know what they are doing) and cocaine (and derivatives thereof).
Quite ironically, I have had very few experiences in person or even anecdotally with one substance, methamphetamine, which happens to be the drug of choice of my estranged father, from whom I am attributed many of my current issues, such as my mental illness, and from whose use of such I am attributed many of my problems stemming from drug use - either by myself or by others. As perhaps a background which could be analysed by those specialised in what I am simply not, the history of drugs and illness as far back as I know in my family is as follows.
My father is a long-time methamphetamine addict who suffers from severely aggravated schizophrenia from his usage.
His father is a still-recovering alcoholic who suffered from an unclear mix-and-match between an autism-spectrum condition and a mostly verbal variation of Tourette's syndrome.
My mother is a non-drug-user who in attempting to relate with me and my father has confessed her experimental usage of cannabis, ketamine, and opium during less obligated days of her youth. She however holds a steady job, supports her family and is not currently addicted to, using, or even likely considering ever doing again, any recreational substance.
Her father, and my immediate grandfather, is also of sound composure currently but has related to me during my times of weakness his own issues with drugs in the past. He claims to have been, in his difficult youth, steadily addicted to prescription drugs and others, namely Tuinal (which has been discontinued).
Amongst the rest of my family, I imagine with some certainty that there has always been, since its induction to American culture, occasional and quite harmless usage of cannabis.
The bread-and-butter of this experience involves my relationship with my partner. We bond very strongly over accepting one-another, and providing comfort and a sense that we have value and purpose. This I believe is what makes us so wonderful together. Though we still have much to learn, our relationship so far has been a learning and growing experience comparable to shaving wood until it fits into another piece. Adjustment and acceptance.
Thusly the pain that I have experienced and currently do so now are two- or ten- or twenty-fold.
And so the story.
My partner, CK, has been under serious stress the past few years because of a variety of issues closing in on him during these difficult years of his life. I may add that he began smoking marijuana when he first met me, and for that I must take some fault in this. Much, perhaps.  At one point of intense anxiety he became unresponsive, and perhaps my bad reaction to it was what ended him up in a mental hospital after the incident. After his admission, his school life was completely destabilized, as it was impractical to stay enrolled in his current school while on an indefinite hiatus for mental health reasons. Therefore on his thankfully prompt discharge from the ward and return to me, he and his family began seeking school settings which would help to minimize his stresses and maximize his productivity. A specialized school located in Manhattan, attended by people from all around New York City and State, was decided the best option due to its special considerations for his demographic.
This, I believe, is where many mistakes began to be made. He began going to school, and I encouraged him to take the opportunity to be at leisure and explore the possibilities of going to school in such a dense yet diverse environment. Immediately, and as I expected and hoped, he began to make friends and develop a rapport with a rather various group of similarly misplaced youths, for some of whom I have truly decided I am affectionate.
Soon, moving on from a 'less mature' group of friends initially, he began to warm up to a certain person I will begrudgingly call by name. She will be called K, and her partner KK. K is a young and talented high-schooler, and she with her partner KK runs a small operation of drug supply and distribution. As far as I know, this includes anything they can get their hands on - however, I know amongst one, the other, or both, there is a preference and on one's side an addiction for the heavy use of and (as a source of income and 'expression') dealing in cannabis and ketamine HCI powder. At first I was completely unaware of these shady dealings; I was under the influence and manipulation of my partner when I believed simply that she and her partner were heavy cannabis users much as I am.
I was under the influence and manipulation of my partner when I believed simply that she and her partner were heavy cannabis users much as I am.
However, as I became more interested in CK's new relationship with K, a new figure took shape as a part of CK's life; K's partner, KK. He is a young adult, severely addicted to ketamine HCI and perhaps other things while using cannabis heavily and regularly. At the very first glance he is a very cut-and-dry, almost 'touchy,' and enigmatic character. He lives a self-professed double life, one under his true name, and another under a pseudonym which makes his severe drug problems seem effectively fashionable to those around him.
A string of events took place, wherein my partner CK became enthralled and seduced so to speak by the supposedly intense and mystical lifestyle of shady deals and fabricated happiness that the pair live by. As they both operate under slangy pseudonyms, are known about the rave scene in NYC, 'party' quite religiously, and at the same time do a marvelous job of communicating themselves to others as accomplished, composed, adjusted individuals who describe themselves as 'bosses' and 'connoisseurs,' I believe that my beloved CK in his time of confusion and weakness decided that he would like to see if this life was for him, as the cheap and 'reliable' idea of putting coins in and getting your satisfaction so perfectly and chemically probably looked like the easy way out of a raw deal. He himself adopted pseudonyms, and began attending these less-than-legal gatherings where he would meet new, fashionable, hip people who he thought he needed more than he needed me. And they all happen to have uncontrollable drug habits.
When I first learned of all these goings-ons, I asked him to tell me the truth. He told me that he would never experiment with drugs because he knew due to my history it would hurt me. He professed so sincerely (I thought) that he could control himself and that his interest in these people was of what he could learn, not what they could sell him and spark him on. This, truthfully, was my mistake to even believe. I already had suspicions that he would begin testing my observance, especially when he had a history of hurting me when it came to drug use and abuse. I knew that he was a hedonist, and is definitely the cat that curiosity killed. I simply felt that any intense mistrust on my part without reliable proof would be damaging to our relationship and decided that I would wait and see. So I allowed him freedom, with of course my warnings and pressures and pleading, to do much as he pleased in Manhattan and its environs, as long as he kept the promise that he would not get sucked into drug use beyond recreational cannabis.
When his cannabis use increased severely as a result of his contact with them, and especially when he began selling cannabis under their wing in large amounts and as an indebted worker, my concerns grew even further but my own guilt to hold him back stopped me from doing what I should have - either giving him an ultimatum or simply dropping him. I feel I was either too weak or too compassionate to do either.
Soon after, perhaps a month or two, we were in bed exchanging affections and discussing life, when suddenly he began to seem disturbed and guilty. He almost began to weep as he told me there was something he had to tell me, but he couldn't bear to for the thought of losing me. I both regret and relish the fact that I pressed him further until he admitted to me the truth.
While cheating on me, he had bought a significant amount of ketamine HCI from KK, and over the course of the week had been repeatedly using and abusing it via insufflation, either as bumps or, sickeningly to me, in large amounts, in lines, to the point where he tearfully admitted that he eventually lost track of how much he was doing and was simply doing it for the fun and the adventure. All the while, he was promising me he wouldn't do so, kissing me, making love, smiling into my eyes while at some points he had a gram of ketamine HCI in his pocket that he simply couldn't be bothered to tell me about.
It began when he was offered some by his idols, these K and KK, and simply couldn't turn it down. Basically directly after his first dosage and experience with it, he decided to buy $40 worth of the illicit substance for his own personal enjoyment and to the ultimate end of my own extreme personal suffering. As I was told this, I harkened back to a moment when I had to physically rip a pipe out of his hand which he was about to smoke, which contained K2 or Spice, a substance he had never tried and didn't even know the background or composure of. This should have been my warning to cut it off or cut him off from such things.
The next week played out as previously mentioned, and meanwhile I regret that I never noticed his increasing behaviors of secrecy, unresponsiveness, distraction, lack of emotional affect, detachment, and depression. He imaginably did more and more every day until at one point, he told me, he actually developed such a tolerance that his regular dosage from the previous week had absolutely 0 effect on him and he was exiting the realms of 'mere' drug abuse and entering the state of constant effort-reward distortion and tolerance-development which are the hallmarks of a serious addiction. Most shaking to me is the speed at which his habit degenerated, as he truly recounted losing sight of his thoughts and behaviors during that 1-2 weeks. He ended up using it with enemies of mine, with the very people he told me he'd never take it from, and even helping K and KK develop their ring of contacts who would buy it from them. He reacted with genuine surprise when I informed him ketamine is a close cousin of PCP, that it can stop one's breathing, that it is intensely addictive, its chemical composure, its history as a date-rape drug and
animal tranquilizer
. He was unaware that it was an anesthetic, unaware of ANY of the far-reaching and immediate affects of its use, and completely oblivious to the way I could subconsciously sense it affecting him during those fateful 2 weeks.
Even now as he claims to be off it completely and even now as I believe him with as much trust remains, he still exhibits signs of ketamine use. He becomes unresponsive more often, panics, cannot explain his emotions (alexithymia) and frequently (ignorantly) speaks of dissociation in his own terms, as if he is not there, does not want to be present, wants to leave, has no emotional responses, and he seems almost delirious with depression and self-loathing. I believe perhaps some of these negative feelings stem from my own intense, tearful, screaming and hurt reaction to his admission and especially his actions. I believe he feels guilt and shame, and for this I am grateful only because it means that he cares. Truth be told, I feel as if I must yet wait for his drugged state to wear off even still, as I feel he is currently still suffering from the effects of his uncontrolled use.  He speaks almost nostalgically, smiling and laughing, of the effects he felt. The numbness all over his body, the feeling of being a spectator out of his body; it made me physically sick, as I can draw parallels between his experience with ketamine and my own experiences with catatonic schizophrenia and especially its affiliated dissociative. I only wonder now what could've truly driven him to do so, as I feel that until he is truly off of it and has truly understood what he has done to himself and to me, I think he is truly incapable of understanding and being fully affected by the gravity of his actions.
I am still uncertain, afraid, angry, hateful, conflicted, confused, and distraught.
I am still uncertain, afraid, angry, hateful, conflicted, confused, and distraught.
I am told by each acquaintance of both mine and sometimes his that I simply shouldn't tolerate him anymore or his betrayal. Yet I realize that if I can survive and accept the fact that my own father has done drugs his whole life and that my life is irrefutably the worse for it, I can survive, accept, and perhaps even come to terms with the fact that my own loved one has insulted all that I stand for by doing the very same thing. The amounts of substance they both did are simply not comparable, but due to their positions in my life and the overarching circumstances, my partner's use of ketamine HCI behind my back has hurt me almost if not even more completely than my father's use of and destruction by methamphetamine. I realize that if I am to understand and deal with my own issues and the things I do in their name, I must learn that others' issues cannot be taken as lesser or lighter than mine. With the half-trusted reassurances by my partner CK that he truly feels terrible for what he did to me and him, and a true gut feeling that he can be guided back toward me and our love for each other, I spend my time now coming to terms with why, and simply HOW I shall go about forgiving him, forgiving my father (as my issues with him are brought back to the surface by this series of events), forgiving myself for letting it get this far, and making something better out of what I have currently.
[Reported Dose: "1g of Ketamine over the course of 2-3 weeks, daily Cannabis 3g or less, Prozac as prescribed "]
